preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each split rule starts with a valid monster ID (1 ≤ mi ≤ n) and a positive integer li (number of resulting monsters/diamonds).

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == li + 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and all(int(x) in {*range(1, n+1), -1} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split()[2:])
preconditions.description: Each split rule has exactly li + 2 integers (mi, li, followed by li integers representing monster IDs or -1 for diamonds).

preconditions.expression: all(any(x == -1 for x in line.split()[2:]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Every split rule contains at least one diamond (-1).
The first line contains two integers m (number of split rules) and n (number of monster types), each between 1 and 10^5.
The sum of li across all split rules is at most 10^5.

postconditions.description: For each monster ID from 1 to n, output exactly one line with two integers (smallest and largest diamonds).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n for line in stdout.splitlines()) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= n for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Output lines correspond to monster IDs in order from 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: all((int(line.split()[0]) == -1 and int(line.split()[1]) == -1) or (int(line.split()[0]) >= 1 and (int(line.split()[1]) == -2 or int(line.split()[1]) <= 314000000)) for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: For each monster, output is either (-1, -1) if no termination is possible, or (min_diamonds, max_diamonds) where min_diamonds ≥ 1 and max_diamonds is either -2 (arbitrarily large) or ≤ 314000000.

postconditions.expression: all((min_d := int(line.split()[0]), max_d := int(line.split()[1])) and (min_d == -1 or (min_d >= 1 and (max_d == -2 or max_d >= min_d))) for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: For each monster, if termination is possible, min_diamonds is the smallest finite number of diamonds achievable, and max_diamonds is the largest finite or unbounded (-2) number of diamonds achievable. If max_diamonds is finite, it must be ≥ min_diamonds.

postconditions.expression: all((monster_id := int(line.split()[0]), min_d := int(line.split()[1]), max_d := int(line.split()[2])) and (monster_id == 1 and min_d == 2 and max_d == -2) or (monster_id == 2 and min_d == 3 and max_d == 4) or (monster_id == 3 and min_d == 2 and max_d == 2) or (monster_id == 4 and min_d == -1 and max_d == -1) for line in stdout.splitlines() if int(stdin.splitlines()[0].split()[1]) == 4 and len(stdin.splitlines()) == 7)
postconditions.description: For the first example input, the output matches the expected results: monster 1 yields (2, -2), monster 2 yields (3, 4), monster 3 yields (2, 2), and monster 4 yields (-1, -1).

postconditions.expression: all((monster_id := int(line.split()[0]), min_d := int(line.split()[1]), max_d := int(line.split()[2])) and (monster_id == 1 and min_d == -1 and max_d == -1) or (monster_id == 2 and min_d == 2 and max_d == 2) for line in stdout.splitlines() if int(stdin.splitlines()[0].split()[1]) == 2 and len(stdin.splitlines()) == 4)
postconditions.description: For the second example input, the output matches the expected results: monster 1 yields (-1, -1), monster 2 yields (2, 2).
